primitives.name: Blocker-Rusher Identification
primitives.verbatim_quote: For the blocker/rusher identification and matchup estimation, we propose two approaches: sequential AutoGluon and graph neural network (GNN) [8-11].
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'B_i': 'Boolean flag indicating if player i is a blocker', 'R_j': 'Boolean flag indicating if player j is a rusher'}
primitives.assumptions: Players are identifiable via sensor data; roles are mutually exclusive per play.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When player positions overlap temporally or spatially without clear distinction.

layer2.mapping: Sequential AutoGluon models map player trajectories and kinematics to binary role assignments (blocker/rusher), analogous to classification kernels in GSI.
layer2.telemetry: Accuracy of 0.99 on test set of ~8,800 plays.

primitives.name: Matchup Estimation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Second, the match-up between blockers and rushers needs to be known to take into account how much resistance a rusher gets when they rush toward a quarterback.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'M_{ij}': 'Binary indicator for matchup between rusher i and blocker j'}
primitives.assumptions: Each rusher-blocker pair is uniquely matched; resistance correlates with physical proximity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When multiple rushers engage same blocker or ambiguous positioning occurs.

layer2.mapping: Graph Neural Network encodes pairwise interactions between rushers and blockers as adjacency matrix; GSE uses this kernel for dynamic state updates.
layer2.telemetry: Average precision of 0.97, recall of 0.91 on test set.

primitives.name: Pressure Probability
primitives.verbatim_quote: Finally, the pressure scores of each rusher and a team needs to be estimated throughout a play.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'P_k^t': 'Probability that rusher k generates pressure at time t', 'T_k^t': 'Time-in-pocket for rusher k at time t'}
primitives.assumptions: Pressure depends on temporal and spatial metrics; modeled as conditional probability given kinematic inputs.
primitives.breakdown_regime: During non-sack, non-hit plays where pressure is inferred but not directly observed.

layer2.mapping: Pressure probability module applies logistic regression on NGS features; GSI computes posterior distributions over pressure events using Bayesian updating.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core innovation lies in extending traditional pass rush metrics beyond final outcomes like sacks or passes made. By leveraging Next Gen Stats (NGS) data and machine learning, the framework identifies blockers and rushers dynamically through sequential AutoGluon and graph neural networks. These models assign boolean flags to players based on their roles during a play, enabling accurate matchup estimation. The pressure probability module then evaluates how much pressure each rusher exerts over time, using kinematic features such as distance and velocity. This allows quantification of pressure even when no sack or hit occurs—addressing a major limitation of existing systems. Dualities emerge between player roles and pressure generation, where a single rusher may influence multiple aspects of play dynamics simultaneously. Failure modes arise from misclassification of roles due to occlusion or sensor noise, leading to incorrect matchup assignments and inflated pressure scores. The framework thus bridges the gap between macroscopic game outcomes and microscopic player behavior.
